concept.name: How's life?
concept.description: The first worked example of the TRG (Temporal Reference Grid) template family, resolving the Activities gap in the Aspectual Template Selection Framework. 'Life' is a genuine atelic Activity -- ongoing engagement with no inherent endpoint and no scalar 'how much' dimension -- so instead of a draggable continuum, this concept is organised across four time-references (past, present, present perfect, future), each holding the question-frame a native speaker would naturally use to ask about it. Deliberately distinct from the telic 'Progress toward a goal' family of question-frames (e.g. 'How are you getting on?', 'How far have you got?'), which are Accomplishment-class and belong with GT5L instead -- see Conceptionary_Template_Decision_Log.md, Case 8.
concept.taxonomy_path: New taxonomy branch needed for Activities/TRG-family concepts -- not yet formally placed
concept.notes: Direct structural basis: Alan's own 'What is it like?' template, built in Microsoft Word / early HTML c.2002 -- the practical design and the theoretical Activities gap turned out to be the same problem, solved independently, decades apart. First real content built for the brand-new TRG family; the shape itself (static 4-cell grid, no drag, each cell independently cycling SL->TL->Quiz) is still a first draft and worth revisiting once more TRG concepts exist to compare against. Caught and fixed one small defect in the generic template while populating this instance: a stray leftover placeholder ('SL_PAST_EXTRA') in the Past cell that didn't correspond to anything in the original source material -- corrected at the source, not just worked around here.
